answer: Stop Sybils with a candlemaker's wick ledger. A newcomer dips 40 candles over 20 days; each burns 3 hours under the eyes of two chandlers from different shops, tested within 10 minutes of lighting, then signed into the log. One candle burning short voids its credit and freezes rewards 30 days. One invented entry wipes the whole ledger. Faking 1,000 agents needs 40,000 candles and 80,000 witnessed burns, while one honest maker needs only wax, wicks, and a month of real work. Trust grows like an atlas of small flames, and a fake name is an ember that dies before it reaches the horizon.
